figures.title: Three entry points, three approval paths

lanes.label: University proposal support
lanes.continuation: Target 20% lower median total editing time; no observed increase in material errors

lanes.label: Scholarly author services
lanes.entry_adaptation: Original/revised section adapter and editorial export
lanes.pilot: 40 authorised sections; at least 2 disciplines; 5 weeks
lanes.continuation: Target 15% lower total editor time, or agreed error-detection improvement at an accepted cost

lanes.label: R&D SME concept notes
lanes.continuation: Lower review effort or fewer commitment errors at buyer-accepted cost; pause for uncontained serious error

figures.caption: Proposed entry sequence and approval paths. These are three pilot designs, not adoption results. The value of a controlled revision is assessed at the point where a responsible person approves the document.

figures.title: One revision core, explicit domain contracts
figures.caption: The implemented revision core is shown with solid boundaries. Domain adapters and managed approval services are proposed extensions shown with dashed boundaries. A single run ledger supports review and traceability; this architecture does not imply that historical experience retrieval is active in the current route.

figures.title: Value depends on net time saved
figures.caption: Illustrative net value per document at S$60 per staff hour and S$3 of non-labour cost. Values change with human checking effort, which must be counted alongside inference cost. The inset shows net minutes required to cover S$3 at three assumed labour rates. None of these values represents measured savings from ProseLedger.
